detects: Local `var` bindings that are never reassigned
disable_if: Your style prefers `var` for locals regardless of reassignment

detects: `late` variables, except `late final` dependency-injection holders
disable_if: Your team accepts `late` with reviewed initialization guarantees

detects: Every postfix null assertion `!`
disable_if: The project accepts `!` after reviewed nullability guarantees

detects: Class methods out of order: getters/setters, `@override`, public, private
disable_if: Your style guide uses a different member order

detects: Variables of a class type whose name does not contain the class name
disable_if: Your naming convention allows short or role-only names

detects: More than one public class, enum or mixin per file
disable_if: Your style allows cohesive type families in one file

detects: String literals in presentation and use-case files that look like user-facing text
disable_if: The project does not localize, or localizes outside these layers

detects: `BuildContext` fields or constructor parameters in view models
disable_if: Never in MVVM code; only if view models intentionally own UI context

detects: Concrete `*UseCase` classes without their own `execute()` returning `Result`
disable_if: Your use cases use another entry point (`call`, a command object)

detects: `dispose()` in view-model-like classes that never calls `super.dispose()`
disable_if: Never for `ChangeNotifier`-based view models

detects: Imports of framework, network, storage, platform or state packages in domain files
disable_if: Your domain layer deliberately depends on one of these packages

detects: `throw`/`rethrow` that can escape use-case or repository methods
disable_if: Your use cases/repositories intentionally propagate exceptions

detects: Flutter UI types declared as fields of `*ViewModel*` classes
disable_if: Your view models deliberately hold Flutter UI objects

detects: Concrete public domain entity/value-object classes without `@freezed`
disable_if: The project does not use Freezed for domain values

detects: Mutable instance fields and public setters in domain entities/value objects
disable_if: Your domain values are deliberately mutable

detects: `fromJson`/`toJson` members or JSON annotations on domain entities/value objects
disable_if: Your domain types intentionally double as wire models

detects: Data models without `fromJson` + `toJson` or a JSON/Freezed annotation
disable_if: Your models use another codec, or some models are not serialized

detects: Concrete `*UseCase` classes under `/domain/useCases/` not extending `BaseUseCase`
disable_if: Your use cases do not share a `BaseUseCase`

detects: Concrete `*ViewModel` classes under `/presentation/viewModels/` not extending a base view model
disable_if: Your view models do not share `BaseViewModel`

detects: Public repository operations not returning `Result` (sync, Future, FutureOr or Stream)
disable_if: Your repositories use another failure protocol

detects: Owned `StreamController` fields not closed on every normal `dispose` exit
disable_if: Never for owned controllers; review borrowed ones instead

detects: Missing type annotations (strict: fields, locals, loops; selective: public boundaries)
disable_if: Your style relies on type inference

detects: Public data-source operations, including interface declarations, not returning `Result`
disable_if: Your data sources throw and repositories convert failures

detects: Use-case/repository construction, `*UseCase.execute()` and complex filters in widget methods
disable_if: Your widgets intentionally hold presentation logic beyond rendering

detects: Static `Map` fields whose value type is a lifecycle resource
disable_if: Never in Flutter UI code; only if no such caches exist

detects: Mixin fields whose type is a lifecycle resource (controllers, timers, focus nodes)
disable_if: Your mixins deliberately own and dispose resources

detects: `dispose()` in UI-state classes that never calls `super.dispose()`
disable_if: Never for `ChangeNotifier`-based UI state

detects: `*UiState` providers listed after `*ViewModel` providers in `MultiProvider`
disable_if: Your composition does not follow the UiState-before-ViewModel naming contract

detects: `DateTime.now()`, local `DateTime(...)`, non-UTC epoch and unconverted `parse`
disable_if: Your project accepts device-local clocks and dates throughout

detects: HTTP client construction/calls and connectivity checks outside network service files
disable_if: Your app has no central network service

detects: Non-UTC `DateTime` construction or parsing in data-layer files
disable_if: Data-layer timestamps are deliberately local or civil dates

detects: Keyless widgets returned directly by `ListView.builder`/`GridView.builder` item builders
disable_if: Your lists are static or items never move

detects: Literal log `context:` values that differ from `Type.member` of the enclosing member
disable_if: Your log context is not a `Type.member` string

detects: `DateTime.toLocal()` calls in presentation files
disable_if: Device-local time is the intended display zone for your app

detects: Civil-date and UTC-instant values combined in one risky expression without an approved helper
disable_if: Your code has no separate civil-date values, or no such mapping folders

detects: Time-pattern formatting of a value not wrapped by an approved company-time helper
disable_if: Your app displays times in UTC or the device zone by design

detects: `unawaited(...)` without a valid `// unawaited-ok: <category> - <reason>` comment
disable_if: Your team does not require justification for fire-and-forget futures

detects: `// ignore:` of the unawaited rules without `// ignore-reason: <reason>`
disable_if: You disabled the unawaited-governance rules

detects: `unawaited(...)` directly inside a Provider `create`/`update` closure
disable_if: Your provider setup never starts async work in `create`

detects: Single-`await` async callbacks in `scheduleMicrotask`, `Timer.run` or `Future(...)`
disable_if: You do not use the unawaited-governance rules

detects: `error`/`warning` calls on `*LoggerService` in data/domain files
disable_if: Your data/domain layers own their error reporting

detects: `warning`/`error`/`critical` logger calls without a structured literal `context`
disable_if: Your logger has no context argument or uses another format

detects: Credential keys in log metadata and credential patterns in log messages
disable_if: Never while logs may persist; only if no such logger exists

detects: Raw exception messages (`error.message`, `e.toString()`) passed to UI text and dialogs
disable_if: Your UI shows backend messages verbatim by design

detects: Raw exception/backend messages forwarded through `??`, message-like arguments or exception constructors
disable_if: Your layers intentionally forward backend messages as user copy

detects: `AppException` subclasses without a `code`, and string-literal `code:` arguments
disable_if: The project has no `AppException` type with stable codes

detects: `statusCode == 401` comparisons outside `AuthInterceptor`/`AuthService`
disable_if: Your auth boundary uses other class names or 401 handling is legitimately local

detects: `*Screen` widgets built by top-level routes that do not extend a `Base*Screen`
disable_if: Your project has no base-screen contract (the rule is then inactive)

detects: Imports of `package:<app>/domain/entities` in screens and widgets
disable_if: The project lets UI consume domain entities directly

detects: `Color(0x...)` hex literals in presentation files
disable_if: The project has no color tokens or theme color scheme

detects: `BorderRadius.circular` with literal 6, 12 or 16 (values with a spacing token)
disable_if: The project has no `AppSpacing` radius tokens

detects: Overlay builders that capture a caller-owned controller or use the caller's `BuildContext`
disable_if: Never in Flutter UI code
